gen-nixie-one-gf-niramit: Nostalgic pencil-thin lines from Nixie One never thicken or thin along a stroke, while Niramit below stays crisp and clean. Retro meets modern.
gen-nixie-one-gf-noto-sans-cypro-minoan: Thin, retro-techy and hairline-steady. Noto Sans Cypro Minoan follows with terminals cut back, leaving big gaps beside Nixie One's identical bars.
gen-nixie-one-gf-noto-sans-javanese: Nixie One draws its strokes like cut ribbon, the same width start to finish, with gaps left open. And Noto Sans Javanese keeps its counters connected to the outside.
gen-nixie-one-gf-noto-sans-kawi: Noto Sans Kawi has a c with open jaws, like a pair of pliers. Nixie One bends its cable-like lines into shapes, while the body simply does the quiet reading work.
gen-nixie-one-gf-noto-sans-linear-a: Nostalgic and a little retro-tech, Nixie One has no modulation anywhere. Noto Sans Linear A sits below with a visibly gaping c, so the two feel related yet distinct.
gen-nixie-one-gf-noto-sans-linear-b: Nixie One looks like laser-cut sheet, every stroke one width, with open curves. Noto Sans Linear B handles smooth, unobstructed bends.
gen-nixie-one-gf-noto-sans-nko: Strokes with no thick-thin swing define Nixie One, and its curves stay open with clear gaps. And Noto Sans NKo adds modern c openings you can see through.
gen-nixie-one-gf-noto-znamenny-musical-n: Noto Znamenny Musical Notation keeps terminals far from the stem. Nixie One's ribbon-like strokes of constant width give it a retro-tech top line, with this body keeping everything modern.
gen-nixie-one-gf-sansation: Sansation reads approachable and neutral, with no ink pooling where its curves turn inward. Nixie One's unmodulated strokes give the pair a nostalgic, retro-tech edge.
gen-nixie-one-gf-sarabun: Retro, thin and wiry. Nixie One is truly monoline, and Sarabun gives it a wide channel into every bowl, so the pair feels clean and approachable.
